Pompliano Unveils AI Wealth-Building Assistant
On Saturday, in a post on
X
, Pompliano criticized the focus of most AI-powered financial products on budgeting and saving money.

"Investors aren’t interested in saving $5 on their coffee purchase," he wrote, arguing that investors want to "grow their investment portfolio, increase their net worth, and create generational wealth."
"Rather than spending less, investors want to make more," Pompliano added.
He mentioned
Silvia, Inc.
, a private AI agent developed by a team of AI engineers to help investors manage and grow their wealth.

According to Pompliano, Silvia can help users "identify investment opportunities, analyze tax-loss harvesting options, find new tax mitigation strategies, think through estate planning" and understand how current events could affect their portfolios.
"I have been using the product for almost two years and it is magical," he said, adding that the assistant also helps him keep track of and better understand his family’s finances.
Pompliano added, "I strongly believe that Silvia can help you and your family as well."
Most AI products in finance are focused on budgeting and saving.

Scott Galloway
and historian
Eliza Filby

params.linkText: financial success increasingly depended on parental wealth

Galloway argued that wealthy parents provided children with advantages through better education, professional networks and financial support, saying, "The most important forward-looking indicator of your wealth, quite frankly, is how wealthy or how rich your parents are."
